newsitem.title: USA: SFE chief expects electricity contract soon.
newsitem.headline: SFE chief expects electricity contract soon.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) chief executive Leslie Hosking said the exchange was within three months of listing an electricity futures contract.
In an interview Thursday at the Futures Industry Association annual conference here, Hosking said the exchange was also "actively developing" coal, water and natural gas contracts.
"We see enormous potential in those energy contracts," Hosking said, citing a deregulation atmosphere in energy markets.
Financial contracts currently account for most of the SFE's volume, but Hosking said he expected energy someday to be as important as financial products.

"We're experiencing the same level of deregulation in the energy markets that everybody else is experiencing," Hosking said, adding that the components that fuel energy production will become valuable futures contracts.
"Water generates electricity in our country and it is also a fairly scarce commodity and as the electricity market deregulates the value of water becomes a variable as well," Hosking said.

Earlier this week, SFE announced a trading floor telephone upgrade project that complements a multi-million Australian dollar local area network upgrade and improved video terminals on the floor, which Hosking hailed as a major commitment to trading floor operations and open outcry.

"I'm not going to fall into the trap and say there is a use-by date on trading floors," Hosking said. But he said the exchange's commitment to screen-based trading technology and innovations was equally important.
